full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiffs in both the suits, in short, was that Moshor Fakir, lit their predecessor, acquired the suit land from landlord-Rafatullah Mondal and had been in possession thereof since 1338 BS as korfa tenant and C.S. Khatian No. 93 in respect of suit land was correctly prepared I in the name of Moshor Fakir. Moshor Fakir while possessing the suit land died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his legal heirs and since his death, the plaintiffs had been possessing the same. The defendants had no right, title and possession in the suit land. On 01.11.1984, defendant No. 2 disclosed to plaintiff No.1 that defendant No.1 executed and registered a kabala in his favour in respect of the suit land and MRR Khatian in respect of the suit land was prepared in the name of defendant No.1, Defendant No. 2 further disclosed that he would build a pucca house therein, Thereafter, plaintiff No.1 went to the local Tashil office and came to know for the first time that the name of defendant No.1 was included in the MRR Khatian along with the name of the plaintiffs father; hence the suit. 

 11. The Appellate Court further found that in the plaint, the plaintiff did not say as to how they exercised their right of possession in the suit land. Though the plaintiff claimed that the defendants dispossessed them from the suit land on 18.11.1984. from the testimonies of the plaintiffs' witnesses, it was clearly proved that long before the said date of alleged dispossession, the plaintiffs were not in possession of the suit land. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that the PWs proved that the defendants had been in possession of the suit land long before the filing of the suit, the defendants' witnesses also said that defendant No. 1 had been in possession of the suit land since 30/35 years, PW1 in his cross-examination stated that Refatullah used to possess the suit land, The Appellate Court further observed to the effect that " উভয় পরে সাক্ষীদের সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনায় ইহা স্পষ্ট বুঝা যায় যে, ১৮/১১/৮৪ তারিখের বহু পূর্ব হইতে নালিশী জমিতে ১নং বিবাদী গেন্দালা দখলকার আছে। অর্থাৎ ১৮/১১/৮৪ তারিখে বাদীকে বেদখলের আর্জি বর্ণিত বক্তব্য সঠিক আছে। The Appellate Court further found that the plaintiff claimed that Moshor Fakir did not give ‘ইস্তফা’ of the suit land to Rafatullah and although the defendants spoke about the ‘ইস্তফা’ they did not file the same, yet PW1 admitted in his cross-examination that the suit land used to be possessed by Rafatullah. The Appellate Court also found that from the evidence of PW1 it was clearly proved that Rafatullah transferred the suit land in favour of his son, Tasiruddin on 19.11.1942 and had he not been in possession of the suit land, he would not have transferred the same in the name of his son and that it was not a believable story that in 1942, Rafatullah would create an ineffective deed in favour of his son thinking about the present suit and that no body would create a fake deed in favour of his son. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that since it was proved from the testimonies of the PWs that the plaintiffs had not been in possession of the suit land for a long time and they had left the suit property long before it could be clearly understood that Moshor Fakir gave 'Estafa' of the suit land in favour of Rafatullah. Therefore, Rafatullah had the right to transfer the suit land. The Appellate Court further observed that from the documentary evidence, it appeared that except the C.S. and the MIRR khatian, the plaintiffs filed only one rent receipt and that also after the filing of the suit, on the other hand, on behalf of the defendants, besides the deeds dated 19.11.1942 in favour of Tasiruddin by Rafatullah, dated 18.02.1948 in favour of Gendala by Moshor and the deed dated 02.08.1960 in favour of Shahjalal, mutation khatian, DCR, 15 rent receipts and the other khatians were filed which also proved the defendants' possession in the suit land. The Appellate Court further observed that the witnesses might tell lie or wrong, but the circumstances do not, the circumstances of case proved that the suit land reverted back to Rafatullah and he transferred the same in favour of his son who in turn sold the same in favour of Gendela, defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 and Mansur purchased the same land from Gendela.
